assays.assay_description: Rats tested individually for 20 min in an acrylic activity box with fresh bedding under 4 lx; 50-kHz USVs recorded via Avisoft CM16 microphone, detected with DeepSqueak 2.6.1 (Faster R-CNN) and manually classified into total, trill, flat and step calls (mixed and 22-kHz excluded from stats). 2x2 design: VEH or LDX (10 mg/kg s.c.) pretreatment 1 h before, VEH or AYA (240 mg/kg p.o.) 20 min before testing. Basal recording on 2nd habituation day.

application_type.evidence: AYA was diluted in water and administered by gavage (p.o.) (LDX co-treatment was s.c., but LDX is not the psychedelic)

setup_habituation.evidence: On two consecutive days, the rats were habituated to the activity box for 20 min.

setup_restrain.evidence: Rats were placed in a clear acrylic activity box (40 × 40 × 40 cm) containing fresh bedding

food_restriction.evidence: They had ad libitum access to standard rat chow and water (home cage); no food described in the activity box during testing.

water_restriction.evidence: They had ad libitum access to standard rat chow and water (home cage); no water described in the activity box during testing.

time_to_assay.evidence: followed by either AYA or VEH (oral) 20 min before behavioral testing in the activity box

sample_size.evidence: n = 12/group; One animal from the LDX +AYA group (total calls =2118) was excluded as a statistically significant outlier from the analysis and graphs.

outcomes.summary: LDX increased total 50-kHz USVs ~10-fold. AYA reduced total, trill, flat and step USVs both under basal conditions and after LDX pretreatment, with the largest reduction in trill calls (LDX-AYA ~18% of LDX-VEH); no pretreatment × treatment interaction.
outcomes.statistics: Total: pre-treatment LR χ2(1)=46.20, p<0.0001; treatment LR χ2(1)=12.03, p<0.0001; interaction LR χ2(1)=0.66, p=0.415. Trill: pre-treatment LR χ2(1)=34.56, p<0.0001; treatment LR χ2(1)=20.53, p<0.0001; interaction LR χ2(1)=0.22, p=0.639. Flat: pre-treatment LR χ2(1)=46.65, p<0.0001; treatment LR χ2(1)=13.39, p=0.0002; interaction LR χ2(1)=1.09, p=0.296. Step: pre-treatment LR χ2(1)=24.33, p<0.0001; treatment LR χ2(1)=7.18, p=0.0070; interaction LR χ2(1)=0.014, p=0.905. IRR LDX-AYA vs LDX-VEH: total 0.372, trill 0.182, flat 0.457, step 0.360; VEH-AYA vs VEH-VEH: total 0.237, trill 0.131, flat 0.260, step 0.391.
outcomes.evidence: AYA treatment reduced the numbers of total 50kHz, trill and flat USV in VEH and LDX-pretreated groups, with a greater effect size in trill calls.

assays.assay_description: Same 20-min session in the 40 × 40 × 40 cm acrylic activity box with fresh bedding; crossings of nine virtual squares and rearings manually counted from infrared video by a blinded experimenter. 2x2 design: VEH/LDX (10 mg/kg s.c.) pretreatment and VEH/AYA (240 mg/kg p.o.) 20 min before testing; correlation and MANOVA with USVs.

application_type.evidence: AYA was diluted in water and administered by gavage (p.o.) (LDX co-treatment s.c.)

setup_habituation.evidence: On two consecutive days, the rats were habituated to the activity box for 20 min.

setup_restrain.evidence: Rats were placed in a clear acrylic activity box... Rat activity was recorded by a 2 MP digital infrared camera

food_restriction.evidence: They had ad libitum access to standard rat chow and water (home cage); no food described in the activity box during testing.

water_restriction.evidence: They had ad libitum access to standard rat chow and water (home cage); no water described in the activity box during testing.

time_to_assay.evidence: followed by either AYA or VEH (oral) 20 min before behavioral testing in the activity box

sample_size.evidence: Data expressed as mean ± S.E.M. and analyzed by two-way ANOVA, n = 12/group.

outcomes.summary: LDX increased crossings and rearings. AYA significantly reduced crossings overall (main effect) but did not attenuate LDX-induced hyperlocomotion and had no significant effect on rearing. Crossings correlated positively with USV counts.
outcomes.statistics: Crossings: LDX F(1,44)=66.80, p<0.001, η2=0.60; AYA F(1,44)=8.80, p=0.005, η2=0.17; interaction F(1,44)=0.709, p=0.404. Rearings: LDX F(1,44)=13.15, p<0.001, η2=0.23; AYA F(1,44)=2.83, p=0.100, η2=0.06; interaction F(1,44)=1.07, p=0.307. Spearman crossings vs total USVs r=0.67, p<0.001. MANOVA crossings×total USVs Wilks' λ=0.69, F(2,43)=9.76, p=0.025; crossings×trill Wilks' λ=0.81, F(2,43)=4.92, p=0.012.
outcomes.evidence: Although AYA treatment significantly reduced the number of crossings, it did not attenuate the hyperlocomotion induced by LDX pretreatment.

B1_num_measures.evidence: recorded as the total number of squares crossed... and the number of rearings

B4_ethological.evidence: the number of rearings (standing on its hind legs for exploration)

B7_automated_classification.evidence: Locomotor activity was manually counted by an experimenter blind to group assignment

B8_multivariate.evidence: Two-way multivariate ANOVA (MANOVA) was used to evaluate the effects of pretreatment and treatment on crossings and USVs.

judge_notes: Kept two assays (USV recording and locomotor/rearing) as all candidates did: same session and apparatus but distinct behavioural domains (affective vocalization vs locomotion/exploration). HPLC neurochemistry excluded as ex vivo.
B1 for USV set to 4-6 (score 2): total, trill, flat, step; gemma's score 3 was inconsistent with its own category.
D2 set to 15-60 min (score 1) for 20-min sessions; gemma's '<15 min' was an error.

D1/D3/D4 scored as multiple sessions/2 days/baseline yes (deepseek4 + gemma majority): paper states basal USV and locomotion were recorded on habituation day 2 'for subsequent analysis' and statistically compared (no differences; data not shown). Confidence medium because data not displayed.
B4 for locomotor assay = Yes (modal): rearing explicitly defined as exploratory behaviour scored as distinct act.
B7 for USV = Yes (unanimous): DeepSqueak Faster R-CNN deep-learning call detection; note subtype classification was manual, so confidence medium.
application_type set to p.o. (AYA route); LDX s.c. is a non-psychedelic co-treatment. Gemma's malformed experimental_conditions block repaired.
USV sample size 47 (min 11) reflects one outlier excluded from LDX+AYA group; locomotor n=48.
Note: paper inconsistently gives box size as 40×40×40 cm (locomotor section) and 30×30×30 cm (USV section); 40 cm used.
